beatOutlines.textOutline: Seeing a fresh all-time high on screen, Raju gets excited.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji immediately warns him to look at the bottom of the chart.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju chased the breakout at ₹148, but trading volume was completely dry.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: As institutional buyers stayed away, price collapsed like a house of cards.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Price told a lie, but volume had already revealed the truth.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In John Murphy's Chapter 7, we decode the deep mechanics of Volume and Open Interest.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: It is critical to see how volume validates trends and sniffs out early reversals.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And finally, practical execution using On Balance Volume and modern variations.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In markets, price is not alone; there is a strict confirmation hierarchy with Volume and Open Interest.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy's rule is clear: Volume and OI are strictly secondary, serving to confirm the price action.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In a healthy uptrend, volume must expand on rallies and contract during pullbacks.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: If price pushes to new highs but volume contracts on each wave, buyers are exhausted.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A classic tenet of technical analysis states: Volume precedes price.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Price looks stagnant on the chart, but unusual volume spikes signal an impending breakout.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Whether top distribution or bottom accumulation, volume points the direction in advance.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Joe Granville engineered On Balance Volume, or OBV, to quantify this cumulative flow.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When the day closes green, entire volume is added; if it closes red, volume is subtracted.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The absolute numerical value of OBV does not matter; only the direction of its slope matters.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When price creates a higher high, but OBV fails to clear its previous peak, that is bearish divergence.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Conversely in bullish divergence, price hits lower lows while OBV forms higher lows, holding ground.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy highlights that an OBV trendline breakout often occurs days ahead of the price breakout.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Classic OBV has a drawback: whether price rises ₹0.05 or ₹50, the entire day's volume is added.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Hence modern chartists employ Volume-Price Trend (VPT) and Chaikin's A/D Line for proportionate weighting.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now your turn. Analyze this market situation.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Think... recall the relationship between price and volume divergence.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Bearish Divergence! Lack of volume confirms a hollow breakout with imminent reversal risk.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: At market close, Raju realized how costly ignoring volume could be.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji smiled and reiterated the deepest trading axiom.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Let us weave the entire essence of Chapter 7 Part 1 into a coherent thread.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Volume must expand along the trend direction and dry up during retracements.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: OBV slope and divergences catch trend reversals well before price confirms.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Modern VPT and Chaikin indicators further sharpen volume weighting accuracy.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Finally discipline and risk management protect your capital in the market.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Remember: Price shows where the market went; volume proves whether anyone believed the move.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Price is Primary, Volume is Secondary confirmation
Healthy trends demand expanding volume in trend direction
Pullbacks on thin volume confirm trend sustainability
'Volume precedes price' highlights smart money accumulation
Joe Granville's OBV tracks cumulative buy and sell pressure
Divergence between OBV and Price warns of market turns
VPT and A/D refine OBV by weighting price change magnitude
Let winning trades run until clear trend reversal appears
bottomTakeaway: Discipline and grounded market understanding are essential for survival.
